method: Independent screenshot-only judgment against all four references. All named images were viewed. Scores consider both resolutions conservatively. No interaction testing is claimed. The Standalone preview banner and unchanged combat room, actor and hand artwork were excluded from comparison. Below-viewport content was not presumed inaccessible. No pair reaches the same-painted-hand standard.

rest.worst_problem: At 1280x800 the third choice ends abruptly inside its panel at the lower content edge; give the choices a physically framed boundary with its cue attached to that boundary.

size_notes.1600x900: The fort and its candle shelf provide an attractive left focal point, but the right panels have blurry, uneven interior treatments and the lower panel is cut by a dark strip. The upper-right utility buttons look like ordinary rounded rectangles.
size_notes.1280x800: The third panel loses its lower explanation at the edge, though More choices below identifies continuation. The detached cue and dark cutoff are less convincing than the richly framed illustration; the rest and sharpen text remain clear.

event.worst_problem: At both sizes the lower parchment choices disappear into a broad dark cutoff that does not read as part of the page support; frame the story viewport and attach its cue to that frame.

size_notes.1600x900: Warm parchment, illuminated initial, enamel choice medallions and cold window light establish a coherent story setting; the third option is visibly cut at the bottom.
size_notes.1280x800: The first two choices remain readable, with the third partially shown above the continuation edge. The illustration and page remain stable, but the support's base and scrolling boundary do not form one believable object.

gameover.worst_problem: At both sizes the enormous central trick card dominates the memorial and is severed before its complete rules, making the summary feel like a cropped inventory display; give the card a complete proportionate display or an explicitly framed detail viewport.

size_notes.1600x900: Portraits and extinguished candle are expressive, but the central card and left/right slabs compete for attention; the left map and central rules disappear beneath a wide dark footer boundary.
size_notes.1280x800: The card rules and left record continue behind the lower cutoff while the right list shows more rows; the More record below cue helps but does not explain the relationship of the three columns. Large unvaried purple textures remain unlike the references' painted staging.

shop.worst_problem: At both sizes the five very tall narrow cards under a mechanically repeated scalloped valance make the shop read as a stretched interface; use naturally proportioned cards on a painted shelf with believable velvet drapery.

size_notes.1600x900: All five visible cards include readable rules, but their deep empty middles and narrow silhouettes are unnatural. The purple valance and backdrop look flat compared with Mr. Moth's painted portrait.
size_notes.1280x800: The five-card layout compresses names and rules into narrower columns; the first BUY remains visible, and the lower category headings plus More wares below indicate continuation. The issue is proportions and material rather than the existence of scrolling.

combat.worst_problem: At both sizes the condition labels along the upper edge have no explicit owner and sit far from their corresponding actor and resource plates; group and label them beside their owners while preserving actor clearance.

size_notes.1600x900: The player's three condition plaques form a wide overhead row, while the opponent's stack is high to the right; text is legible and avoids the main actor silhouettes, but ownership is only inferred from position. The plain How to play rectangle remains a conspicuous mismatch.
size_notes.1280x800: The player labels become a stack at the far upper left, separated from the child and companion; the opponent stack remains high right. The plates, bars and resource panel are clear, but the ownership problem is more pronounced.
size_notes.comparison: No meaningful UI difference among the four combat pairs justifies a visual preference. Actor poses, room rendering and unchanged hand artwork were excluded from comparative judgment; the shared background score is descriptive only.

ranking_notes.combat: All four are visually tied on the assessed UI; listed in inspection order solely to satisfy the ordered schema.
ranking_notes.rest: SAPPHIRE and PERIDOT are close; SAPPHIRE's quieter material wins over PERIDOT's stronger full-width cue treatment.
ranking_notes.event: SAPPHIRE, PERIDOT and AMBER are close. Dedicated clean boundary space favors SAPPHIRE, while PERIDOT's oversized footer bars and AMBER's floating cue weaken staging.
ranking_notes.shop: SAPPHIRE and PERIDOT are close; SAPPHIRE has the quieter velvet atmosphere, while PERIDOT has the clearer ornamented continuation boundary.

winner_rationale: GARNET offers the most consistent dark painted materials, the strongest physically staged shop, and named scroll boundaries that remain understandable at both sizes. Its rest panels and memorial surfaces are quieter than the alternatives, and its shop's continuous wooden shelf and embroidered velvet are closest to the reference hand. It still falls short of reference fit: the memorial's oversized card, overlay-like boundary strips, sharp badge rendering and ownerless combat condition labels remain material defects.
winner_fixes: Combat, upper condition groups at both sizes: add a compact owner name or portrait medallion and position each group in a dedicated lane beside its owner, clear of actor silhouettes, guard crests, health/name plates and the left resource panel.

Gameover, central card display at both sizes: preserve the enlarged rules text but show a complete naturally proportioned card in a dedicated framed detail region; give the memorial portraits and extinguished candle more focal authority.

Gameover, right Final Tricks viewport at 1600x900: stop the visible region after a complete row or add a deliberate framed reveal edge; the partial next-row names should not appear chopped by the cue strip.

Event, lower Story Register boundary at both sizes: confine it to a believable page or easel support and paint a carved lower lip with contact shadow, rather than laying a room-wide strip across the background.
Rest, cost badges at both sizes: integrate the rectangular amount plaques into the choice frames with softer antique-gold edge highlights, patina and shared directional light.
Rest, lower Fort choices boundary: give the named strip the thickness and corner treatment of the choice furniture while keeping its cue in reserved space clear of text and the exit control.
Shop, card feet and price tags at both sizes: add coherent contact shadows on the continuous shelf and soften the uniform bright card outlines so their painted depth matches the velvet and wood.
All noncombat headings: replace the hard white-and-gold outline effect with subtly shaded, worn engraved lavender lettering consistent with the reference title and nameplates.
Combat, upper-right How to play control: replace the plain rounded rectangle with the same antique-gold cartouche treatment already used by the rest screen's utility controls.

grafts.idea: Borrow the fully framed, explicit Continue through wording as an affordance, but keep GARNET's restrained material and local viewport width instead of stretching a cartouche across the whole room.
Borrow the especially quiet deep burgundy shadowing in the curtain interior while retaining GARNET's continuous shelf and embroidered valance.

Retain the idea of showing a small glimpse of the next merchandise category headings below the first display, when available space permits; preserve GARNET's natural card proportions and enlarged rules.
